summary:
IGNIS is an AI-powered platform designed to improve our understanding of fire behavior in microgravity and support safer space exploration.

The project combines NASA combustion experiment data, machine learning models, and a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system to analyze fire behavior and make scientific research more accessible. Through an interactive dashboard, users can explore experimental results, examine model predictions, and ask questions about NASA research papers.

IGNIS aims to help researchers identify potential fire risks, understand existing research gaps, and support the development of safer habitats for future missions to the Moon and Mars.
details:
IGNIS processes NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) research data to provide insights into combustion behavior in microgravity. We selected 24 NASA investigations and developed an ETL pipeline that transforms experimental measurements from different formats into a unified dataset of 1,947 test records, with standardized units and traceable data corrections.

The platform combines several AI components. Machine learning models, including Random Forest classifiers and regression models, analyze combustion outcomes, burning rates and flame behavior. A Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system indexes 93 scientific documents into 4,631 searchable passages, using semantic embeddings and keyword retrieval to answer research questions with source citations.

We also developed an explainable scenario-ranking system that compares NASA experiments against different habitat conditions, including the ISS, Moon and Mars. An interactive 14-page dashboard built with Streamlit brings these capabilities together, allowing users to explore experiments, compare results, simulate scenarios and identify research gaps.

The project was developed primarily in Python, using scikit-learn, NumPy, ONNX Runtime and Streamlit, with optional Google Gemini integration for AI-generated answers.

IGNIS is designed to bridge the gap between scientific research and practical fire-safety insights, supporting the development of safer environments for future space missions.
